# Micro-interactions

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

Presses, toggles, checks, ripples, badges and the small tells that make an interface feel touched. 39 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Skeleton placeholders hand over to content

`dv-skeleton-load` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy calm · any

Cards first appear as blank or blurred slabs with grey bars for text (or a code panel with only its line numbers, or avatar circles), then the real content resolves in layers: the pin first, the text, then the photo; a selection dot pops last.

- **Build:** Cards with a skeleton face cross-switched to the content face (HardStep per layer). Anatomy: Blank slab 2-4 f; layers 2 f apart; gutter 26 f before the first code pixel. Sound: UI pops on each card.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** Hand-off 28 f; per card 4-6 f.
- **Use when:** Loading states; anything the product fetches or generates.
- **Avoid when:** Skeletons that last longer than about 0.5 s.

### CTA peeks in cropped, then cuts to centred

`dv-cta-peek-centre` · logo and end card · accent · energy calm · launch

A call-to-action tag peeks in at the edge of a grid, cropped, and creeps wider for about a second; hard cut to the tag centred and whole, breathing.

- **Build:** Cards with a creep, then a cut to a centred Card with Oversize from 1.04. Anatomy: Peek creep 52 f; cut; breathe 24 f expo-out. Sound: A kick on the cut.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** 96 f.
- **Use when:** Ending on a registration or sign-up.
- **Avoid when:** Long peeks.

### Tiny labels pop in mirrored pairs and drift out

`dv-mirrored-label-pairs` · layout and composition · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

Ten tiny metric labels pop in pairs mirrored about the centre and drift outward slowly.

- **Build:** Words pairs with mirrored x and an outward drift. Anatomy: Pairs 2-3 f apart; drift outward. Sound: None.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** Pairs over 25 f; drift 36 f.
- **Use when:** Surrounding a hero number with context.
- **Avoid when:** Labels that must be read.

### Chip bloom around content

`mi-chip-bloom` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch, vertical

A container grows out of its content: a dropped icon tile widens into a labelled chip that floods with the accent and wipes back to an outline, or a solid pill swells behind a name so the group becomes a button.

- **Build:** Tile to chip: on the drop, scale the tile 0.8 to 1 over 8 f E.out. Then tween the pill width from the tile width (equal to its height) to the label width plus padding over 12 f E.out. On the same progress, the icon slides to its left slot and the label reveals with a clip-path inset from the right. A flat C.accent fill clipped to the pill is erased by a mask-image linear-gradient with an 80 px feather, sliding left to right over 20 f E.outSoft and leaving a 1.5 px border. Bloom behind: an absolutely positioned pill behind the text (radius height/2, C.ink fill) tweens from the text bounds (measureTracked) to the bounds plus 48 px on each side over 10 f E.out. Meanwhile the text mixes from C.ink to C.white over 6 f, starting on the bloom's second frame. Hold the finished chip at least 18 f before it does anything else.
- **Timing:** Tile pop 8 f E.out; widen 12 f E.out; fill wipe-off 20 f E.outSoft with an 80 px feather; bloom behind 10 f E.out with a 6 f text inversion; hold at least 18 f.
- **Use when:** An integration, tag or name should become a tangible, clickable object (attached, added, now a button), shown as cause and effect.
- **Avoid when:** The fill would need several hues to read, or the chip has nothing to do next (a bloom with no follow-up reads as decoration).

### Chips and tags pop in place

`dv-chip-pop-in-place` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy calm · any

Tags with coloured status dots, secondary chips, an inline file chip in a prompt or a notification dot simply appear at full saturation in one frame, one every few frames: no fly-in.

- **Build:** HardStep visibility per chip. Anatomy: One-frame cut-on; 2-6 f apart; an inline chip appears as one token. Sound: None, or within another pop.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HardStep`
- **Timing:** 1 f each; gaps 4-12 f.
- **Use when:** Secondary UI that should not compete with the hero motion.
- **Avoid when:** Popping the hero element (give it an entrance).

### Click answered by a colour pulse, not a bounce

`dv-click-colour-pulse` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy calm · any

On the click the pointer vanishes and the button's fill ramps through a light tint and lands in its new state (with a check, an "Analyzing" label, a popover from its tail); or the colour drains upward through the button as its arrow launches; or the button flashes white and blurs for 3 f before turning to the active colour.

- **Build:** press() q drives a colour interpolation; HardStep for the white flash; springBox from the button for the popover. Recipe: background linear-gradient(0deg, next 0 %, current 66 %), background-size 100 % 300 %, background-position-y stepping 0 -> 100 % inside each 4 f state. Anatomy: Hover 8 f, click, colour ramp 9-23 f, hold, fade; popover pops from its tail in 3 f. Sound: A bubble pop at -1.2 dBFS plus a wood-block; a UI pop. Materials: The fill changes colour by a vertical gradient climbing through it: each new colour enters at the bottom edge and pushes upward through a soft gradient 1.5x the button's height, about 4 f per state through a short hue walk, then holds 18 f and fades in 6 f.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Materials:** The fill changes colour by a vertical gradient climbing through it: each new colour enters at the bottom edge and pushes upward through a soft gradient 1.5x the button's height, about 4 f per state through a short hue walk, then holds 18 f and fades in 6 f.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Hover 12-19 f; ramp 12-23 f; popover 10 f in, 7 f out.
- **Use when:** Send, copy, export, confirm.
- **Avoid when:** A second multi-hue ramp in the same film.

### Click feedback: dot, ring, tint

`dv-click-ripple-dot` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy calm · any

On click a small dot blooms at the cursor tip, a thin ring expands around it to about 40 px, and the clicked area takes a light tint that holds.

- **Build:** Build: <Ripple at x y color shape={{ w, h }}> (fx/MicroUI): an 18 px dot blooms (2 f), a thin ring grows 10 -> 40 px (12 f, E.snapOut) and the clicked area takes a 14 % tint that holds (6 f). Anatomy: Dot 18 px, ring 10 -> 40 px fading, area tint over 6 f. Sound: A soft UI tap on the ring.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MicroUI.Ripple`
- **Timing:** 26 f in all; ring 12 f.
- **Use when:** Clicks on flat areas without a button shape.
- **Avoid when:** Glow halos (keep the ring thin).

### Click to focus: I-beam, ring, caret

`mi-field-focus-caret` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch, vertical

An arrow cursor turns into an I-beam as it enters an empty field and clicks. The field's border sharpens, a caret appears and blinks twice at an uneven, human pace, and on the first key the placeholder vanishes and the pointer fades away.

- **Build:** Draw the I-beam as a variant of src/fx/Cursor.tsx: a 2.5 px C.ink stem 28 px tall with 9 px crossbars over a 2 px C.white outline, using the arrow's drop shadow. Its stem centre, not a tip, sits on the hotspot, and it scales about that point. The arrow travels on cursorArc and swaps to the I-beam in one frame, on the fd(f) where its tip enters the field's rect, arriving 8-12 f before CLICK. On CLICK (pressAt) the field takes focus: its border goes from 1.5 px C.line to 2 px C.ink through mixColor on prog(f, CLICK - 1, CLICK + 4, E.ui), so the change shows on the press frame, with no halo. On the same frame a 0.08 em x 1 em caret appears at the start of the text, while the C.mute placeholder stays where it is. Blink the caret on a hard, uneven table decided with fd: on 18, off 16, on 24, off 12 f, then the first key at CLICK + 70 (or just on 18, off 16 when the beat is tight). The pause should read as a person gathering a thought, never as a metronome. On the first key the placeholder vanishes in one frame, TypeOn takes over with a solid caret, and the I-beam fades out over 8 f on E.smooth, because a system pointer hides while typing. Run one log-space push toward the field under the arrival and the blinks (lc between two shots in src/lib/camera.ts, up to about 1.8x over 40-44 f on E.cam), so the wait is never a still frame. Put one 'click' at weight 0.3 on CLICK and no sound on the blinks.
- **Timing:** Arrive in 24-36 f on E.smooth, 8-12 f before the click; glyph swap 1 f; press 4 f down, 8 f recoil; focus border 5 f E.ui from CLICK - 1; caret blink in hard steps of 18/16/24/12 f (70 f) or 18/16 f (34 f); placeholder gone in 1 f on the first key; I-beam fade 8 f E.smooth; push up to 1.8x over 40-44 f E.cam.
- **Use when:** A shot opens on an empty prompt, search or chat field and the first action is typing into it, so the click into the field becomes the cause of everything after.
- **Avoid when:** The field is already focused or pre-filled, the product acts on its own with no cursor, or the film has already played the full two-blink wait once (later prompts start at the first key).

### Drag, lift and seat

`mi-drag-lift-seat` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy medium · walkthrough, feature, vertical

A chip or file picked up by the cursor lifts off the surface, follows the hand with a slight lag and tilt, then drops into its slot with a small contact squash as the slot accepts it.

- **Build:** On the grab (pressAt), scale the item 1 to 1.04 and deepen its shadow from 0 2px 4px to 0 16px 32px at 18% black over 8 f E.out. While dragging, place it at the cursor path evaluated at f - 3 (a 3 f lag). Tilt it by rotateZ = clamp(vx * 0.25, -6, 6) degrees, where vx is the cursor's horizontal speed. When it enters the slot, thicken the slot outline from 1 to 2 px and tint it over 6 f E.ui. On release, run the last 40-80 px into the slot on E.contact over 8 f and settle the scale and shadow back. Apply squash(t) anchored at the contact edge, and put a 'snap' or light 'land' on the contact frame.
- **Timing:** Lift 8 f E.out to 1.04 with a 16/32 px shadow. Follow lag 3 f; tilt at most 6 degrees. Slot tint 6 f E.ui. Drop 8 f E.contact, plus squash over about 8 f.
- **Use when:** A drag-and-drop (attach a file, add an integration, reorder a card) causes the next state.
- **Avoid when:** The drag path is long (over about 600 px, cut it), or the item contains text that must be read while it tilts.

### Pill grows around its label

`dv-pill-label-build` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy calm · any

A pill builds around its words: an outlined pill pre-sized per phrase with words cut on inside it; a link icon first, then words, the outline widening symmetrically; a label pill growing up from its bottom edge beside a tile.

- **Build:** Morph box width from the measured text (FontGate); words pop inside. Anatomy: Words 4-6 f apart; width eases with each word (or pre-sized); growth from the bottom edge on an expo-out. Sound: A bubble pop and a mouse click 80-140 ms after.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** 10-20 f per pill; words 10-15 f apart.
- **Use when:** Labels, tags, prompt chips.
- **Avoid when:** Text that spills before the pill grows.

### Press: squeeze, hold, snap home

`ui-press-grammar` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy any · any · also `dv-press-squeeze-release`

A button squeezes in on an in-out curve, holds for a beat, and releases accelerating back to exactly its size, with nothing above rest afterwards; the click sound sits on the first frame of the squeeze.

- **Build:** press(f, at, {}, film).scale on the button's transform (or <Card press={{ at }}>); q drives the colour snap or the shadow. The cursor's own press dip and ring (Cursor press, cursorRing) start on the same frame.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards.press`
- **Materials:** The press can bend its container: see the jelly press for the edge displacement, and the button fill can change colour by a gradient climbing through it rather than a cross-fade.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** x0.87 (0.86-0.90; a big tile 0.81); 9 f down on M.press, 3 f held, 10 f release on E.buildIn.
- **Use when:** Every click the film shows.
- **Avoid when:** Never bounce a button past its size; that is the one spring's job.

### Selection bar slides to the clicked item

`dv-sidebar-nav` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough

On click the cursor shrinks a little and a solid selection bar slides down the sidebar to the clicked item while the page cross-dissolves in 3-4 frames; a group expands its sub-items and pushes the items below down.

- **Build:** snapBox/E.snapOut on the bar's y; Cards stack for the group. Anatomy: Bar 8 f; dissolve 6-8 f; sub-items open in 12-16 f pushing 110 px. Sound: A UI click.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** 8-16 f.
- **Use when:** App navigation in a walkthrough.
- **Avoid when:** Pages that slide (they cross-dissolve fast in real apps).

### Send as a ghosted handoff

`mi-send-ghost-handoff` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, vertical

On send, the composer's text drifts up and fades away while the same content appears above as a posted message, briefly overlapping the old text, instead of flying between containers.

- **Build:** From the send press, fade the composer text over 12 f using q = prog(f, send, send + 12, E.smooth): opacity 1 - q, translateY -12 * depart(q) px, and blur blurOut(q, 4), so it only softens once it is moving. Starting 4 f after the press, bring the posted bubble in at its final place over 18 f, with opacity on E.smooth and translateY 12 to 0 px through arrive(prog(..., E.out)). Empty the composer on frame +12 and bring its placeholder back over 8 f. Pair it with the press envelope on the send button.
- **Timing:** Composer out over 12 f E.smooth (-12 px, blur up to 4 px). Bubble in over 18 f from +4 f (12 to 0 px, E.out with arrive). 8 f of overlap; placeholder back over 8 f.
- **Use when:** A message, prompt or post is submitted and the result appears elsewhere in the same frame; this is calmer and cheaper than a flight.
- **Avoid when:** The journey itself is the point (show the flight), or the move would serve as a transition between shots, where a crossfade is never the default.

### Shared highlight walks the menu

`mi-shared-highlight-walk` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, vertical

One rounded highlight slides from row to row of a sidebar or menu, trailing the cursor, and the chosen row settles into a pale accent tint.

- **Build:** Render a single absolutely positioned highlight behind the rows: radius 8 px or row height / 2, C.white on a dark sidebar, C.mist on a light one. Tween its translateY and height to each target row's rect, taken from the layout data, over 12 f E.out, starting 4 f after the cursor reaches that row. Walk about 24 f per row; the first hover can appear in one frame. On the click, mix the chosen row's background to C.accent at 10% opacity over 8 f E.ui and its label to C.ink, then fade the moving highlight over 8 f. The row text never moves.
- **Timing:** 12 f E.out per hop; about 24 f per row; trails the cursor by 4 f; click tint 8 f E.ui; highlight fade 8 f.
- **Use when:** Navigation through a menu, sidebar or list should read as a small human decision, with spatial continuity.
- **Avoid when:** The rows are too small to read at the shot's framing (push in first), or a soft radial bloom would be added to the highlight.

### State changes in place without travel

`dv-state-change-in-place` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy calm · any

A control changes state the way software does: a toggle turns on without sliding (the knob dissolves on the left and reappears on the right while the brand colour switches in the same frame); a header label clears and the new label appears as the chevron slides to its width; sub-panels swap content on one frame; a frosted bubble is a solid button after a cut.

- **Build:** Build: <Toggle at mode="inPlace" w track trackOn knob> (fx/MicroUI): the knob dissolves on the left and reappears on the right while the track switches in one frame at the midpoint (26 f); other in-place swaps stay HardStep / stepValue with the chevron on a short E.snapOut. mode="spring" (house) crosses on SPR.landing clamped at 6 % with the track snapping 1 f after the click. Anatomy: One-frame swaps; the only eased part is the chevron or the colour. Sound: A state-change sound. Materials: A chip's label changes by the new label sliding in from the right inside the pill while the old one is clipped (both overlap for 4-6 f, about 20 f per swap); a phone screen can change content by a 6-8 f ghost dissolve (old 100, 50, 20, 0 %) while the device moves.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MicroUI.Toggle`, `fx/HardStep`
- **Materials:** A chip's label changes by the new label sliding in from the right inside the pill while the old one is clipped (both overlap for 4-6 f, about 20 f per swap); a phone screen can change content by a 6-8 f ghost dissolve (old 100, 50, 20, 0 %) while the device moves.
- **Timing:** 1 f swaps; label change 16 f; toggle 26 f.
- **Use when:** Toggles, status labels, panels switching.
- **Avoid when:** Tweening what software would switch.

### The caret waits and blinks

`dv-caret-beats` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy calm · any

The placeholder clears and a thick caret waits about 6 frames before typing starts; after typing, the caret blinks while the bar lifts away.

- **Build:** TypeOn caret with a pre-hold and blink. Anatomy: Caret 6 x 45 px; hold 12 f; blink on/off 16 f. Sound: None.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn`
- **Timing:** Hold 12 f; blink period 32 f.
- **Use when:** Before and after any typing.
- **Avoid when:** A caret that blinks during the typing.

### Toast or chip arrives smeared or blurred, then sharpens

`dv-toast-chip-entry` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy medium · any

A status chip enters sideways as a horizontal smear (a thin streak, then a smeared pill, then sharp); a notification grows from a blurred pill and rises; a toast pops blurred at the push's midpoint, rises and sharpens; a disc inflates behind an icon (the icon leads); a tab bar slides down as the scroll brakes.

- **Build:** Cards enterState with defocus (two ladder copies) and a 1-2 f horizontal ghost. Anatomy: Streak 1 f, smear 2 f, sharp; growth 1136 -> 1408 px in 7 f; rise 17 px; the disc starts 2-4 f after its glyph. Sound: A chat pop or wood-block on the cut; a soft note after whooshes.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** 8-24 f.
- **Use when:** Status messages, notifications, small UI pieces arriving.
- **Avoid when:** Long smears on readable text.

### Two-beat confirm cascade

`mi-two-beat-confirm-cascade` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, vertical

A row of buttons or toggles confirms one by one: the label or knob changes first, the fill follows a beat later, and the rows go at uneven, human gaps.

- **Build:** Give the rows irregular start frames, never a metronome: for example [0, 4, 19, 37] for four toggles, or [0, 10] for two buttons. Button: swap the label at t0, with a 4 f crossfade or a 6 f roll (the old label rises 8 px and leaves, the new one enters from 8 px below through arrive()). Then mix the background from C.ink2 to C.accent over 8 f E.out, starting at t0 + 12. Toggle: slide the knob 0 to 20 px over 8 f E.out with no overshoot, and mix the track from C.line to C.accent over 10 f E.smooth from the same frame. Put a light 'tick' (weight 0.25-0.35, panned by x) on each state change.
- **Timing:** Label 4-6 f; fill 8 f E.out at +12 f. Knob 8 f E.out; track 10 f E.smooth. Row gaps such as 4, 15 and 18 f.
- **Use when:** Several integrations, permissions or capabilities switch on, and each confirmation must stay legible at video speed.
- **Avoid when:** There is only one control (use the press envelope), or every row would start at the same interval.

### Badge count bump

`mi-badge-count-bump` · micro-interactions · accent · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, loop, vertical

A notification badge or counter chip ticks up: the digit rolls to the next value while the badge gives a small pulse, once per increment.

- **Build:** Draw the badge as a pill (C.accent fill, C.white tabular-nums digit) with the digit in an overflow-hidden slot. On each increment frame c, roll the old digit up and out and the new one in from below, one line height of travel over 8 f, with arrive(prog(f, c, c + 8, E.out)). Pulse the badge scale to 1 + 0.12 * hitPulse(f - c, 2, 5), and retween its width over 8 f E.out when the digit count changes (9 to 10). The badge first appears from its icon's corner (transformOrigin there) on SPR.micro. Space increments unevenly, at least 12 f apart, with a 'tick' of weight 0.3 on each.
- **Timing:** Digit roll 8 f E.out; pulse hitPulse(t, 2, 5) x 0.12; width 8 f E.out; first appearance on SPR.micro; increments at least 12 f apart, uneven.
- **Use when:** Incoming activity (messages, leads, approvals) should register as small, countable events on the UI.
- **Avoid when:** The count is the hero number of the shot (use a full counter), or increments would come faster than about one per 12 f.

### Cursor vanishes into an outlined button

`dv-cursor-becomes-button` · micro-interactions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

On click the cursor disappears and an outlined circle with an arrow appears at about 111 % and settles, as if the click produced the button.

- **Build:** Cursor visibility off on the click + Oversize from 1.11. Anatomy: One-frame swap; settle expo-out. Sound: None distinct.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cursor`
- **Timing:** 16 f.
- **Use when:** A call to action at the end of a demo.
- **Avoid when:** Keeping both cursor and button.

### Drag-select snaps glyph by glyph

`mi-drag-select-highlight` · micro-interactions · accent · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

An I-beam presses at the start of a phrase and drags across it, a tinted highlight grows behind the text one whole character at a time, and on release a small action bar grows out of the selection, ready for the product to act on it.

- **Build:** Measure the line once under FontGate: px[k] = measureTracked(text.slice(0, k), size, weight, track) for every k, so the highlight snaps to real glyph edges. Park the I-beam on boundary a and press with pressAt at DOWN. Then drag it to boundary b along x = lineLeft + mix(px[a], px[b], prog(f, DOWN + 2, DOWN + 2 + D, E.smooth)), with D = max(24, 2 x (b - a)) f, so the cursor stays at or under 12 px/f. The selection end is the boundary nearest the cursor, decided on fd(f): k is the index in a..b that minimises |px[k] - x|. The highlight therefore jumps one glyph at a time and never tweens, and that stepping is what makes it read as a real selection. Draw it between the field and the glyphs (layer order: field, highlight, text, cursor), from px[a] to px[k] at full line height with a 3 px radius, in mixColor(C.paper, C.accent, 0.22), keeping the text C.ink. On a dark stage use solid C.accent with C.white text, but only if the accent means 'chosen'. Release the press 6 f after the last step. 4 f later, grow an action bar 12 px above the line from the selection's top centre: transformOrigin at its bottom centre, scale lmix(0.05, 1, prog(f, UP + 4, UP + 14, E.out)), opacity over its first 4 f. For the follow-up, either remove the range in one frame (highlight and glyphs together, with the rest of the line closing up through the measured layout) and type the replacement in from px[a] with TypeOn, or restyle the selected glyphs in place. To select a whole word, use a double click: two presses 8 f apart select it in one step on the second press.
- **Timing:** Drag about 2 f per glyph (24-40 f) on E.smooth, cursor at 12 px/f or less; highlight steps per glyph on whole frames; release 6 f after the last step; action bar 10 f E.out from +4 f; hold at least 36 f before the edit; replacement typed over about 26 f; double-click presses 8 f apart.
- **Use when:** The product acts on a piece of text the user picks (rewrite, translate, comment, format, ask about a passage), and the pick should read as a human choice rather than a preset.
- **Avoid when:** The text is under about 40 px tall at the shot's framing (push in first), the range spans more than two lines, or the cursor never touches text anywhere else in the film.

### Focus ring: pop on click, trim to point

`mi-focus-ring-pop-or-trim` · micro-interactions · accent · energy any · feature, walkthrough, launch, vertical

A thin outline around a control either pops outward and fades the moment it is clicked, or draws itself clockwise around a target and erases from the tail, pointing at the action without a cursor.

- **Build:** Draw an SVG rounded rect around the control's bounds, with rx equal to the control radius plus the outset, a crisp 2-3 px stroke and no blur copy. Pop mode: on the press frame, grow the outset from 4 to 14 px with prog(..., E.out) over 8 f and fade the stroke from 0.9 to 0 linearly over 20 f. For a handoff, keep the ring at 14 px instead so it becomes the border of the next element (an alert card, or the frame of the next shot). Trim mode: 6 px outset, dasharray '10 8', masked by a second rect with pathLength 1 that shows only the run from tail to head (strokeDasharray `${h - t} 1`, strokeDashoffset -t). Here head = prog(f, s, s + 24, E.smooth) and tail = prog(f, s + 24, s + 48, E.smooth). Repeat on the next target about 108 f later while the cursor rests nearby. Use C.accent for the stroke only when the accent's one meaning is 'act here'; otherwise use C.ink on light stages and C.white on dark ones.
- **Timing:** Pop: outset 4 to 14 px in 8 f E.out; opacity 0.9 to 0 over 20 f, linear from the press. Trim: draw 24 f and erase 24 f, both E.smooth (a 48 f loop); dashes 10/8 px, 3 px stroke; next target about 108 f later.
- **Use when:** A click needs a visible result the next shot can build on, or a calm frame must point at the next action without moving a cursor.
- **Avoid when:** The cursor already sits on the target (the ring is redundant), or the ring would need a glow or blurred halo to read.

### Hover pulse on contact

`dv-hover-pulse` · micro-interactions · accent · energy calm · any

When the cursor touches a button its rim grows about 8 % in 2 f and decays back over 4 f.

- **Build:** Build: hoverPulse(f, at) (fx/MicroUI) on the rim's scale: +7.8 % in 2 f at 30 fps, back over 4 f. Anatomy: Scale +7.8 % in 2 f, decay 4 f. Sound: None, or a faint tick.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MicroUI.hoverPulse`
- **Timing:** 12 f at 60 fps.
- **Use when:** Before every important click.
- **Avoid when:** Continuous pulsing.

### In-place character rewrite

`mi-in-place-char-rewrite` · micro-interactions · accent · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

A small monospace status field is overwritten left to right by its new state, or a sensitive value turns to dots and deletes from the right, all inside the same fixed slot with no layout change.

- **Build:** Set the field in FONT.mono with whiteSpace pre so every character keeps its column. Overwrite: k = fd(prog(f, s, s + 12, E.linear) * max(oldLen, newLen)) and text = next.slice(0, k) + prev.slice(k). Start it 8 f into the press release, so the status changes as the button's light fades. Optionally lift a companion icon 10 px over 4 f E.out and bring it back over 8 f. Redact: on the click frame, swap the value to '•'.repeat(n) in one frame, then set n = len - fd((f - s) / 2) so one dot deletes every 2 f. Meanwhile, an anchor-camera pan over 40 f E.inOut keeps the toggle icon centred; put the click on a downbeat.
- **Timing:** Overwrite at about 1 character per frame (13 characters in 12 f), linear, starting 8 f after the press peak. Redact: 1 f swap, then 1 dot deleted every 2 f; camera pan 40 f E.inOut.
- **Use when:** The product's own status (sending, receiving, connected) or a privacy claim should change in place and read as the machine's voice.
- **Avoid when:** The text is decorative rather than real UI status (it becomes filler text), or the field uses a proportional face, so the columns jump.

### Input with a moving coloured border

`dv-gradient-border-input` · micro-interactions · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A dark rounded input whose border light travels around its outline in two brand colours, continuously.

- **Build:** A conic-gradient border (a baked plate) rotated by transform. Anatomy: Conic border rotated continuously. Sound: None.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform; light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo
- **Timing:** Continuous (68 f per turn).
- **Use when:** An AI input in a brand that owns that look.
- **Avoid when:** House films (it reads as the stock AI look).

### Launch hop that never lands

`mi-launch-hop` · micro-interactions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A centred app icon hops up as if launching, hangs at the top for a beat and starts to fall, and the camera leaves before it lands, so the hop motivates the scene change.

- **Build:** Chain the icon's translateY with tw: 0 to -77 px over 10 f E.outSoft, hold 4 f, then -77 to +20 px over 18 f E.contact (gravity, ending with velocity), with no squash. Scale a soft contact shadow from 1 to 0.85 and fade it as the icon rises. Start the scene change (a camera tilt-away, a whip or a cut) on frame 14, the first frame of the fall, so the landing never resolves on screen.
- **Timing:** Rise 77 px in 10 f E.outSoft; hold 4 f at the top; fall 18 f E.contact; the camera leaves from frame 14; 32 f in all.
- **Use when:** Opening the app or launching a feature should motivate the move to the next scene with a familiar OS gesture.
- **Avoid when:** The icon must come to rest in the same shot (then it needs a real landing), or several icons would hop in turn.

### One-element tell before the event

`mi-pre-event-tell` · micro-interactions · accent · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch, loop

Just before a state change or a cut, exactly one small thing moves, such as a plus glyph turning 45 degrees into an x or an object slowly turning toward its target, while everything else holds.

- **Build:** Plus mode: rotate the plus glyph 0 to 45 degrees with prog(f, cut - 16, cut - 6, E.smooth) so it finishes 6 f before the cut. Repeat it before every result cut so the viewer learns the tell. Yaw mode: rotateY the object 0 to 35 degrees over 40 f E.linear inside perspective 1200px. The camera tail creeps at most 0.1% scale per frame and nothing else changes; fire the event (a 2-4 f impact or a hard state change) on the frame the yaw ends. The tell is the motion of the shot, so keep it to one element and add no cursor.
- **Timing:** Plus: 10 f E.smooth, finishing 6 f before the cut. Yaw: 40 f linear to 35 degrees, with the event on the next frame; camera creep at most 0.1% per frame.
- **Use when:** A repeated result cut, or a sudden 2-4 f event, needs anticipation so it reads as caused rather than random.
- **Avoid when:** Several things already move in the frame (the tell gets lost), or the yaw would leave the rest of the frame static for more than 48 f.

### Pill marquee; selected pills fill

`dv-pill-marquee-select` · micro-interactions · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

Rows of outlined pills with words alternate with small line icons, scrolling as a marquee; the selected pills fill with colour from their left end, connectors draw between them, the rest dim.

- **Build:** Wipe kind 'feather' inside each selected pill; connectors as stroke draw-ons. Anatomy: Fill left-anchored 16-24 f; connectors 20 f; dim 18 f. Sound: Voice. Materials: The chosen outline pill fills with a horizontal gradient (a pale tint at its left end, the accent at 45 %, a near-black shade at its right end) revealed by width over about 20 f, under white text; its 2 px outline stays visible.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Materials:** The chosen outline pill fills with a horizontal gradient (a pale tint at its left end, the accent at 45 %, a near-black shade at its right end) revealed by width over about 20 f, under white text; its 2 px outline stays visible.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** 175 f in all.
- **Use when:** Choosing among modes or capabilities.
- **Avoid when:** Gradient fills in house films.

### Radial dash burst around a word

`mi-radial-dash-burst` · micro-interactions · accent · energy high · launch, sting, vertical

Short dashes burst outward around a hero word on the beat, drift almost imperceptibly while it is read, then fly outward faster as the frame pushes into the cut.

- **Build:** Place 22 rounded rects (4x20 px) around the word at angles from rand(`dash${i}`), oriented radially, in C.ink at 60-80% opacity. Their radius is r = 187 + 87 * prog(f, b, b + 16, E.out) + 0.5 * max(0, f - b - 16), plus 176 * prog(f, cut - 20, cut, E.in) in the last 20 f while the camera pushes in. The motion-blur pass smears the burst and the exit. Start it on the beat the word lands.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Replace the random dashes with 12 evenly spaced radial ticks (every 30 degrees, 20 px long, 3 px stroke, C.ink, one SVG) forming an ordered ring around the word. Drive them with the same radius curve: 187 to 274 px in 16 f E.out, a 0.5 px/f drift, then out to about 450 px over the last 20 f E.in. It reads as a graphic emphasis mark rather than debris. A single 2 px ring stroke on the same curve also works. The full look relies on particles, confetti; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Burst +87 px in 16 f E.out; drift 0.5 px/f for about 50 f; exit +176 px over the last 20 f E.in into the cut.
- **Use when:** A single hero word on a beat needs a physical punch.
- **Avoid when:** The text is body copy, the shot is UI, or the burst has already been used once in the film.

### Round button with a liquid fill and a rim

`dv-liquid-glass-button` · micro-interactions · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A round button with a thin up-arrow, a bright rim highlight and an accent liquid fill pooled at its bottom; it shrinks with the pull-back, pulses on hover and implodes on click.

- **Build:** Layered circles with a baked rim plate. Anatomy: Rim highlight, liquid pool, glyph. Sound: None. Materials: At rest the round glass button holds a swirling liquid in its lower third and a streak across the top; as the cursor approaches the liquid swirls up and fills the sphere (18 f), on touch it drains to a thin layer (16 f); fill blobs blurred about 10 px inside a hard circle mask, a white inner highlight at 30 %, a rim glow about 8 px. The arrow inside scrolls out of the top (8 f, ease-in), the button is empty for 4 f, and a fresh arrow rises from the bottom (8 f, ease-out), landing as the cursor touches.
- **Materials:** At rest the round glass button holds a swirling liquid in its lower third and a streak across the top; as the cursor approaches the liquid swirls up and fills the sphere (18 f), on touch it drains to a thin layer (16 f); fill blobs blurred about 10 px inside a hard circle mask, a white inner highlight at 30 %, a rim glow about 8 px. The arrow inside scrolls out of the top (8 f, ease-in), the button is empty for 4 f, and a fresh arrow rises from the bottom (8 f, ease-out), landing as the cursor touches.
- **Conditions:** glass as a material with real frost or refraction, not a default card style
- **Timing:** Static; implodes in 6 f.
- **Use when:** A hero button in a brand with a glass language.
- **Avoid when:** House films.

### The field bends like jelly where it is pressed

`dv-jelly-press` · micro-interactions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

As the cursor presses a button inside an input card, the card's edge and corner bow outward round the button (a soft bulge, the corner radius swelling), the edge goes slightly wavy along its length, then everything springs back.

- **Build:** Recipe: the rounded rect as an SVG path sampled at about 80 points, displaced each frame in closed form. Anatomy: Edge displacement d(s) = A exp(-(s - s0)^2 / (2 x 120^2)) along the normal, A peaking about 9 px at 1080p; a ripple of 2 px sin(2 pi s / 90 px - phase); stroke and shadow follow the shape; the cursor squashes 1 -> 0.8 -> 1 with it. Sound: The click, then a wood-block.
- **Timing:** Bulge 6 f, wobble 10 f, release 4 f.
- **Use when:** The one press of a film that should feel physical; playful brands.
- **Avoid when:** Serious enterprise tools; every click.

### A tiny seed square appears first, then unfolds

`dv-seed-square-unfold` · micro-interactions · signature · energy medium · any

A 15-40 px coloured square appears exactly where something will land and sits for 1-4 frames, then bursts into a photo tile, slides and widens with each typed character into a sticky note, stretches into a label bar whose text types, or a line end becomes a capsule that unfolds centre-out into a labelled card.

- **Build:** Build: <Seed at box color mode="burst"|"stretch"|"capsule">{content}</Seed> (fx/Seed): a 24 px square cut on at the landing spot, held 4 f, then burst (expo-out from a third of the way, 14 f), stretch (a bar of the label's height, 20 f) or capsule (centre-out, then open, 17 f); widths for a note that widens per typed character; seedOnsets(start, n) for a run every 4-6 f. Anatomy: Seed square (2-4 % of the frame) -> hold 1-4 f -> expo-out to the full box starting at a third; width follows typing instantly; capsule widens centre-out revealing its letters. Sound: A glockenspiel note on the first seed; none per seed after.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Seed`
- **Timing:** Seed 2-8 f; tile 12-16 f; new tile every 4-6 f; bar stretch 20 f; capsule 14-20 f.
- **Use when:** Building a layout tile by tile; labels and notes; any arrival that should feel planted.
- **Avoid when:** Seeds that do not match the final element's colour.

### Anticipation dip before an unlock

`mi-anticipation-dip-unlock` · micro-interactions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

Light builds on a locked card, the card briefly darkens as the lock's shackle swings open, then it pops to clean full-tone content, so the release feels bigger than it is.

- **Build:** Drive the card wrapper's filter brightness through a tw chain: 1.0 to 1.5 over 14 f E.in (the build), then 1.5 to 0.8 over 12 f E.out (the dip). On the pop frame, swap the locked art for the clean art in one frame (decided with fd), hidden inside the brightness pulse, never crossfading the two. Set brightness to 1 + 0.35 * hitPulse(t, 3, 6) and scale to 1 + 0.024 * hitPulse(t, 4, 4): a pulse, not a spring. During the dip, rotate the shackle -30 degrees about its hinge (transformOrigin at the hinge point) with E.out and lift it 4 px. Repeat it faster on a second card (a 7 f pop instead of 12 f) so the second read is snappier, and put a 'pop' or 'snap' event on each pop frame.
- **Timing:** Build 14 f E.in to 1.5x. Dip 12 f E.out to 0.8x, with the shackle at -30 degrees. Pop 12 f (7 f on the repeat) with a hitPulse(t, 3, 6) brightness pulse and a 2.4% scale pulse. About 38 f in all.
- **Use when:** Something locked, gated or hidden becomes available (an unlock, a reveal, access granted) and the moment should land as a payoff.
- **Avoid when:** The brightness would clip whites into a bloom, or the film already has two big payoff beats.

### Integration icons slide in and pin to the pill

`dv-integration-orbit-pins` · micro-interactions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

Five app-icon tiles appear one by one around a central pill as each is named, and matching coloured dots pin to the pill's border, so the connections read.

- **Build:** Cards enterState per icon + small dots placed on the pill's border by angle. Anatomy: Slide about 16 f expo-out; onsets tied to the words; dots at the border points facing each icon. Sound: Each icon lands with its word.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** 86 f for five.
- **Use when:** Integrations, connected sources.
- **Avoid when:** More than about six icons.

### Selection handles appear, drift and resize

`dv-selection-handles` · micro-interactions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

Four small square handles appear one by one clockwise around a subject and drift outward; they pull in until they overlap the corners, then spring back past rest; the cursor becomes a corner-bracket handle and drags a translucent selection rectangle; handles snap around a small word and the selection grows to swallow the cards around it.

- **Build:** <Markers boxes onsets blink> for the handles; the drag as a Morph box tied to the cursor. Anatomy: 24-32 px squares; appear 2-3 f apart clockwise; drift 47 px out; overlap then spring past rest; selection rectangle at 25 % white with corner marks. Sound: None, or soft ticks.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Markers`
- **Timing:** Appear 32 f; drift 30 f; spring 15 f; drag 20 f.
- **Use when:** Editing and selection tools; pointing at the subject of the film.
- **Avoid when:** Handles in a film without an editing idea.

### Send button launches

`dv-send-button-launch` · micro-interactions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

The round send button detaches from its box and launches on a J-curve toward the camera (drifting right while rising and growing), or its arrow rotates to point back and flies along the input, erasing the text with a liquid smear.

- **Build:** Recipe: x on E.snapOut, y on E.buildIn, scale linear; the erase is a Wipe whose edge follows the arrow. Anatomy: x peak early, y peak late (J), diameter growing linearly; arrow rotate 90 deg on an ease, fly on an ease-in, a smear erasing behind it. Sound: A kick on the launch, a whoosh on the exit; or a silence then a sub-drop. Materials: The button that flew away comes back: about 2 s later a white disc spins in from a frame corner, motion-blurred (rotational smear for 6 f), and settles into the send slot of the new window (12 f, strong ease-out) on a sub drop.
- **Materials:** The button that flew away comes back: about 2 s later a white disc spins in from a frame corner, motion-blurred (rotational smear for 6 f), and settles into the send slot of the new window (12 f, strong ease-out) on a sub drop.
- **Timing:** Launch 42 f; rotate 17 f, fly 26 f.
- **Use when:** The moment a request is sent.
- **Avoid when:** Sending without consequence (the next shot must show the result).

### Stretchy tab indicator

`mi-stretch-tab-indicator` · micro-interactions · signature · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, loop, vertical

The selected pill of a segmented control shoots to the new option with its leading edge arriving first, stretches to about 1.9x its width mid-travel, then hugs the new label as the label takes the active colour.

- **Build:** Animate the indicator's leading and trailing edges as two tweens on the same E.glide: the leading edge reaches the target edge in 12 f and the trailing edge in 20 f. Width = right - left therefore swells to about 1.9x near frame 6 and relaxes into the target width. Keep the height fixed, the radius at height / 2 and the fill flat. Mix the new label from C.mute to the active colour over the last 8 f, and the old label back over the first 8 f. Step the new label's weight from 500 to 600 on the landing frame with fd. Calm variant: fade the fill to a 1.5 px outline ring over the first 6 f. Swell the ring to 1.35x by 30% of the travel and shrink it onto the target by 100%, over 48 f E.smooth, then snap the solid fill back over 4 f on landing. Put a tick on the landing frame.
- **Timing:** Leading edge 12 f, trailing edge 20 f, both E.glide, for hops up to about 250 px. For longer hops keep the 0.6 ratio and lengthen both so the leading edge stays under about 65 px/f (a 420 px hop takes 18 f / 30 f). Label colour 8 f. Calm variant: 48 f E.smooth, 6 f fill fade, 4 f snap.
- **Use when:** A tab, filter or toggle switch causes the next state (the chart changes, the list swaps) and deserves weight.
- **Avoid when:** The control has more than about five options in a tight row (the stretch overlaps its neighbours), or the indicator would only read with refraction or a frosted backdrop behind it.

### The one spring: a container pops open

`ui-one-container-spring` · micro-interactions · signature · energy medium · launch, update, feature, vertical · also `dv-one-spring-pill`

The film's single overshoot: on the click, the container (a button becoming its confirmation, a pill becoming a menu) springs open past its size and settles; nothing else in the film overshoots.

- **Build:** springBox(f, start, { A: button, B: confirmation }, film) drawn as one rounded box (or <Card spring={{ start, from }}>); fade the new label in over the first 15 f. Name the element class in timeline SPRING_CLASS.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards.springBox`
- **Timing:** SPR.landing (zeta 0.59, about 10 % over, home in 23 f at 60 fps); start it on the click or one or two frames before the container is seen.
- **Use when:** The one moment the product answers the user.
- **Avoid when:** Type, logos that already move on a curve, or a second class of element in the same film.

### Velocity-stretch dot

`mi-velocity-stretch-dot` · micro-interactions · signature · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch, loop

A small round dot (a cursor or a list marker) stretches into a capsule along its motion in proportion to its speed, anchored at its trailing end, and shrinks back to a dot when it stops.

- **Build:** Compute the head H(f) from an eased path, clamped to its start position before the move. Compute the tail as a pure-function exponential follow: T(f) is the sum over i = 0..29 of 0.8^i * H(f - i), divided by the sum of 0.8^i, which gives a lag of about 4 f. Draw an SVG line from T to H with strokeLinecap round, strokeWidth equal to the dot diameter, a flat fill and no shadow. Size it at 3.3-5.3% of frame height for a cursor (C.white on dark), or 18-21 px for a list marker (C.accent). Marker mode: drop it in from the top edge over 31 f E.out, so it arrives as a long streak that shortens into the dot. Hop it 54 px to the next item over 22 f E.smooth on a 54 f cadence, with the active label mixing from C.mute to C.ink over 8 f around the hop midpoint. Exit by stretching it into a dash about four times the dot's length (about 84 px for a 21 px marker) over 17 f on E.smooth, then shoot it off with E.in. The stretch is the streak, so draw nothing behind it.
- **Timing:** Tail weights 0.8^i over 30 f (a lag of about 4 f): length about rest + 4-5.5 f x speed, back to a dot in 16-20 f. Marker: drop 31 f E.out; hop 54 px in 22 f E.smooth every 54 f; label colour 8 f; exit: stretch to an ~84 px dash over 17 f (E.smooth), then off on E.in.
- **Use when:** A tiny element must lead the eye across a slab or down a list, and needs speed, direction and character.
- **Avoid when:** UI truth requires a standard system arrow, or several dots would stretch at once (the trick only reads once).
